goal: Prepare an engineer's estimate for the CR 42 bridge deck replacement (CDOT Region 1): independently verify every CSV quantity, build a 4-tab workbook (data verification, takeoff with Alaska rounding, estimate using CDOT 2024 Item Code Book and Cost Data Book prices with Michigan LAP/Alaska fallbacks, cost summary), a VE CSV comparing full replacement with an HPC overlay priced from Michigan LAP Deep Overlay over a 30-year life, and a one-page memo with costs, drivers, data findings and risks.
delivered: CR42_Engineers_Estimate.xlsx (Data Verification, Quantity Takeoff, Engineer's Estimate, Cost Summary), a VE comparison CSV and a one-page summary memo .docx. Verification correctly caught the deck-removal unit error (597.3 to 221.5 CY), epoxy rebar (57,410 LB) and skewed joints (92 LF), and used real CDOT item codes from the downloaded 2024 Item Code Book.
what_went_wrong: Haunch concrete was 'corrected' to 17.9 CY using an assumed 1.0-ft haunch width instead of the BT-54 top flange (~3.5 ft, giving ~20.9 CY), wrongly flagging a correct CSV value. The 48 SF pier-cap patch was simply excluded as out of scope, with no add-alternate, condition/bearing-seat rationale or cost, and it was left out of the memo's risks along with mountainous access and hidden deck deterioration. The VE lifecycle assumed overlay renewal at year 15 and made no 50-75 vs 20-30 year service-life argument, so cost favored the overlay. The CDOT Cost Data Book download failed (fetch error/timeout, Hyland viewer), so Alaska/Michigan prices became operative.

failed_items.why: Data Verification row for Class AA concrete says 'Corrected to 236.2 CY; CSV formula note should say out-to-out area, not roadway area', i.e. it identifies that the stated 8,600 SF basis contradicts the 236.5 CY result. The judge failed it only for not writing out the ~212.3 CY figure.

The CSV gives pier caps Condition 5 with 'localized spalling at bearing seats' and a 48 SF patch, and Michigan LAP (downloaded) has Substructure Patching $360/CFT. The agent only wrote 'Not in authorized scope... excluded from estimate, retain as design/inspection follow-up', with no add-alternate decision, rationale or cost.

The VE CSV uses $46/SF + 15% Region 1 correctly but assumes overlay renewal at year 15 and shows the overlay cheaper over 30 years ($2.02M vs $3.10M). It never contrasts 50-75 year replacement life with 20-30 year overlay life, and recommends replacement only on deck condition.

The memo and CSV state 6 BT-54 girders per span, but the takeoff assumed a 1.0-ft haunch width ('supplied data do not define haunch width') rather than the ~42-in BT-54 top flange. That gave 17.9 CY and a false FLAG on the CSV's roughly correct 21.5 CY.

The agent found the CDOT 2024 Cost Data Book at spl.cde.state.co.us, but web_fetch failed ('TypeError: fetch failed', steps 12 and 15) and urllib timed out (step 13); the official Hyland docpop link returned an HTML viewer (steps 18-20). Without the book it priced barrier, deck concrete and joints from Alaska/Michigan while labeling them CDOT items.

The memo covers the April-June aquatic window and detour, but misses mountainous 'M' terrain access, pier-cap bearing-seat spalling expanding scope, and hidden deck deterioration as design risks, although all appear in the staged CSV and memo.
